byteward.sentence: Hackers stole data from 9 million TicketRiver accounts, the ticket seller said on Tuesday.
The company says it has hired an outside security firm to investigate.
The stolen data includes names, email addresses, phone numbers, and hashed passwords.
TicketRiver says no payment card numbers were taken.
Every TicketRiver user will have to reset their password the next time they log in.

launch-desk.sentence: TicketRiver says a breach exposed 9 million customer accounts.
The company will pay for 2 years of credit monitoring for affected customers.
TicketRiver shares fell 9% in afternoon trading.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: TicketRiver has confirmed a breach affecting 9 million accounts.
They logged in with a password stolen from a contractor who handled customer support.
TicketRiver found the intruders on October 28.
TicketRiver hashed them with an outdated method that a modern graphics card can crack quickly.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Attackers accessed 9 million TicketRiver accounts, the company said on Tuesday.
It disclosed the breach in a regulatory filing.
According to the filing, TicketRiver discovered the intrusion on October 28.
TicketRiver is offering affected customers 2 years of free credit monitoring.
Two customers have already filed a class-action lawsuit over the breach.
